concept: cpi inflation consumer prices gdp growth national accounts indec
official_series: Consumer Price Index for Greater Buenos Aires (CPI-GBA) and GDP, INDEC
what_happened: INDEC changed its CPI staff and methods from 2007. The IMF Executive Board issued a declaration of censure on 1 February 2013 over the CPI-GBA and GDP data, and lifted it on 9 November 2016 after a new CPI.
effect_on_data: The IMF found the CPI-GBA and GDP data did not meet Argentina's reporting obligations; official inflation and real growth for 2007-2015 are not comparable with independent measures or with the post-2016 series.
cross_check: Provincial CPIs published by statistics offices outside INDEC, such as the City of Buenos Aires index.

concept: cpi inflation consumer prices central bank statistical centre divergence
official_series: Consumer price index, Central Bank of Iran (CBI) and Statistical Centre of Iran (SCI)
what_happened: The CBI withheld its CPI from the Iranian month Azar (Nov-Dec 2018) onward, and in January 2019 a commission of the Statistical High Council ruled that the CBI had no mandate to publish price indices or national accounts.
effect_on_data: Two official CPIs diverged before the halt (Aban 1397: 39.9% y/y at the CBI versus 34.9% at the SCI), and while it lasted only the SCI series was published. The CBI's inflation page now shows annual inflation for every year from 1397 (31.2%) onward, with a base-year change at 1401; the page does not say when the 1397-1400 figures were published.
cross_check: None licence-clean.
source_name: Eghtesad Online (news report; the CBI's current series is at cbi.ir/Inflation)

concept: gdp gnp national accounts growth multinationals intellectual property leprechaun gni star
official_series: Gross Domestic Product and Gross National Product, Central Statistics Office (CSO)
what_happened: In July 2016 the CSO reported real GDP growth of 26.3% for 2015, driven by multinationals relocating intellectual property assets. The CSO then introduced Modified GNI (GNI*), first published in July 2017.
effect_on_data: GDP and GNP include large multinational IP, aircraft leasing and redomiciled-company flows; in the CSO's first estimate 2016 GDP was EUR 275.6bn against GNI* of EUR 189.2bn, so GDP ratios understate debt and other burdens.
cross_check: GNI* and Modified Domestic Demand, both published by the CSO.

concept: exchange rate official rate parallel market lira dollar multiple rates banque du liban
official_series: Official exchange rate LBP per USD, Banque du Liban (BDL); USD-denominated aggregates converted at it
what_happened: After the 2019 crisis the official rate stayed at 1,507.5 LBP/USD until February 2023, when it moved to 15,000, and then to 89,500 in January 2024, per Banque du Liban. In its 2023 Article IV staff report (Country Report 23/237) the IMF recommended unifying the multiple exchange rates.
effect_on_data: The official rate was far from the rates at which most transactions took place, so any series converted to or from US dollars at it, including GDP and balance-sheet aggregates, is misstated for the period.
cross_check: None licence-clean.
source_name: Banque du Liban, Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Report 2024

concept: public debt external debt guaranteed loans hidden debt fiscal accounts
official_series: Public and publicly guaranteed external debt, Ministry of Economy and Finance; IMF and World Bank debt series
what_happened: In April 2016 the authorities confirmed to the IMF state-guaranteed external borrowing that had not been disclosed; the IMF put it at US$1.4 billion, about 10.4% of GDP.
effect_on_data: Debt and fiscal figures published before April 2016 omit these loans, so vintages from 2013 to early 2016 understate public debt.
cross_check: Post-2016 IMF debt sustainability analyses and World Bank International Debt Statistics vintages.

concept: public debt government debt oil-backed loans traders hidden debt cemac
official_series: Public and publicly guaranteed debt, Republic of Congo authorities; IMF staff estimates
what_happened: After a March 2017 mission at which, an IMF spokesman later said, Congo had not fully disclosed its debt, an IMF mission in October 2017 estimated public debt at end-July 2017 at CFAF 5,329bn (about US$9.14bn), around 110% of GDP.
effect_on_data: Debt figures published before the October 2017 estimate, including the March 2017 figure, understate public debt; the revised figure still excluded litigated debt and domestic arrears accumulated since 2014.
cross_check: Post-2017 IMF debt sustainability analyses and World Bank International Debt Statistics vintages.

concept: foreign trade exports imports trade partners customs commodity balance
official_series: Foreign trade statistics, Federal Customs Service (FTS)
what_happened: The FTS suspended trade statistics in April 2022. In March 2023 it published 2022 totals by commodity group, without a partner-country breakdown (last published for January 2022), and said releases would follow monthly about 40 days after each period. Publication then paused again and resumed in November 2023 with January-September 2023 data broken down by region, not country (TKS.ru, 14 November 2023).
effect_on_data: Customs trade by partner country is missing from February 2022, and commodity data is published only at a coarse level and irregularly; February to December 2022 had no official monthly release at the time.
cross_check: Partner-country mirror statistics, such as Eurostat Comext and other partners' published imports from and exports to Russia.
source_name: Interfax (news report; the Federal Customs Service site could not be reached)

concept: oil production crude gas condensate output energy rosstat industrial production
official_series: Crude oil, natural gas and condensate production, Rosstat
what_happened: Government Order No. 1074-r of 26 April 2023, made under Federal Law No. 55-FZ of 28 February 2023, suspended publication of oil, gas and condensate output, monthly from March 2023 and quarterly from the first quarter of 2023, initially until 1 April 2024; Rosstat's industrial report omitted them.
effect_on_data: Official monthly and quarterly oil and gas production figures are missing from March 2023.
cross_check: OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report secondary-source estimates of Russian crude output.
source_name: Reuters (via Kitco; the official texts on pravo.gov.ru and rosstat.gov.ru could not be reached)

concept: public debt fiscal deficit government debt hidden loans audit waemu
official_series: Central government debt and fiscal deficit, Ministry of Finance and Budget
what_happened: A February 2025 audit by Senegal's Court of Auditors covered 2019-2023 budget execution. The IMF said it confirmed significant underreporting of fiscal deficits and public debt.
effect_on_data: The IMF reported end-2023 central government debt revised from 74.4% to 99.7% of GDP, including undisclosed loans of 25.3 points of GDP, and the 2019-2023 average deficit revised up by 5.6 points of GDP.
cross_check: Court of Auditors audit figures and post-audit IMF estimates.

concept: gdp growth national accounts inflation reserves balance of payments data gaps
official_series: National accounts, prices and external sector data, State Committee of Turkmenistan on Statistics and Central Bank of Turkmenistan
what_happened: In September 2026 the IMF Executive Board found Turkmenistan in breach of its data obligations for not providing reserves, gold and FX holdings and a full balance of payments. A 2023 IMF working paper rebuilt its GDP because official national accounts are weak.
effect_on_data: Key external-sector data are not reported, and the IMF's working paper notes that weak national accounts tend to show overstated growth; official growth and price figures cannot be checked against complete underlying data.
cross_check: Night-time lights, such as EOG VIIRS and NASA Black Marble, and partner-country mirror trade for gas exports.

concept: inflation cpi gdp national accounts balance of payments central bank data blackout
official_series: Consumer prices, GDP and balance of payments, Banco Central de Venezuela (BCV)
what_happened: The BCV published no inflation or GDP data for periods after 2015 until 29 May 2019, when it released figures including 130,060% inflation for 2018 and a 22.5% fall in GDP in the year to the third quarter of 2018.
effect_on_data: There is no official contemporaneous data for 2016 to early 2019; the later releases are retrospective and could not be checked against published data at the time.
cross_check: IMF World Economic Outlook staff estimates and OPEC secondary-source oil output.
source_name: Central Banking (trade press; no BCV release or IMF document stating this could be reached)

concept: gdp growth autocracy dictatorship night lights satellite overstatement
official_series: Real GDP growth as reported by national authorities
what_happened: A 2022 study (Martinez, Journal of Political Economy) compared reported GDP with satellite night-time lights across countries and found that autocracies report higher GDP growth for the same growth in lights than democracies.
effect_on_data: The study estimated that autocracies overstate yearly GDP growth by approximately 35%; official growth for non-democracies should be read as an upper bound.
cross_check: Night-time lights growth, such as EOG VIIRS and NASA Black Marble, for the same country and period.
source_name: Journal of Political Economy (University of Chicago Press)

concept: re-exports sanctions circumvention mirror trade bilateral exports imports partner country russia intermediated
official_series: Merchandise trade by partner country, national statistics offices of Armenia, Kazakhstan and the Kyrgyz Republic
what_happened: An EBRD working paper (No. 276, February 2023) found that after EU sanctions on Russia from March 2022, direct EU exports to Russia fell sharply while EU exports to Armenia, Kazakhstan and the Kyrgyz Republic rose, most for sanctioned goods.
effect_on_data: Partner-country trade figures for these economies include goods that pass on to Russia, so bilateral flows overstate final use in the reporting country and understate trade with Russia.
cross_check: Exporter-side mirror statistics, such as Eurostat Comext EU exports to each country.
source_name: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

concept: remittances personal transfers migrants cross-border transfers russia tajikistan kyrgyzstan uzbekistan
official_series: Cross-border Transfers of Individuals in Breakdown by Countries, Bank of Russia
what_happened: The Bank of Russia's statistics page for cross-border transfers of individuals, including the breakdown by country, lists annual files only up to 2021.
effect_on_data: Sender-side figures on transfers from Russia to Central Asian countries are missing from 2022, when flows changed most, so recipient-country figures cannot be checked against Russian data.
cross_check: Recipient central-bank inflow data (National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic, National Bank of Tajikistan, Central Bank of Uzbekistan).

concept: government debt deficit augmented off-budget lgfv local government financing vehicles fiscal borrowing
official_series: General government deficit and debt, Ministry of Finance of the People's Republic of China
what_happened: Alongside general government figures, the IMF's 2024 Article IV consultation reports an augmented measure that adds borrowing by local government financing vehicles and other off-budget funds.
effect_on_data: For 2024 the IMF projected general government debt at 60.5% of GDP and augmented debt at 124.0%; augmented net borrowing was 13.2% of GDP against 7.4% on the general government basis.
cross_check: IMF Article IV augmented deficit and debt tables, published annually in the China staff report.

concept: gallium germanium exports customs export controls licensing critical minerals trade shipments
official_series: Exports by HS commodity code, General Administration of Customs of China
what_happened: MOFCOM and the General Administration of Customs announced on 3 July 2023 that exports of listed gallium and germanium items would need a licence from 1 August 2023 (Announcement No. 23 of 2023).
effect_on_data: Monthly export lines for the controlled codes track licence approvals rather than demand or output; customs data showed no gallium or wrought germanium exports in August 2023, after several tonnes in July.
cross_check: Partner-country import statistics for the same HS codes (Eurostat Comext, UN Comtrade mirror data).
source_name: Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China

concept: gdp growth national accounts investment savings local government statistics nbs
official_series: Gross domestic product, investment and saving, National Bureau of Statistics (NBS)
what_happened: A 2019 study in Brookings Papers on Economic Activity (Chen, Chen, Hsieh and Song) found that local statistics misrepresented activity more after 2008, without a matching change in NBS adjustments.
effect_on_data: The authors estimated that 2008-2016 GDP growth was about 1.7 points a year lower than official figures, and the 2016 investment and saving rates about 7 points lower.
cross_check: Electricity generation, rail freight volumes and partner-country imports from China.

concept: youth unemployment jobless rate 16-24 labour survey students nbs
official_series: Surveyed urban unemployment rate by age group (16-24), National Bureau of Statistics (NBS)
what_happened: The NBS stopped publishing age-group unemployment after the June 2023 figure of 21.3% and resumed in January 2024 with a series that excludes students, giving 14.9% for December 2023.
effect_on_data: There are no figures for July to November 2023, and the series excluding students is not comparable with the earlier one.
cross_check: None licence-clean.
source_name: State Council of the PRC (Xinhua, reporting NBS)

concept: exchange rate parallel market black market devaluation egyptian pound usd conversion unification
official_series: Official EGP/USD exchange rate, Central Bank of Egypt
what_happened: The Egyptian pound was devalued in several steps from 2022 while foreign-exchange shortages persisted; in March 2024 the official and parallel rates were unified under the IMF-supported programme.
effect_on_data: Before unification the official rate was below the market price of dollars, so series converted to USD at the official rate (GDP, wages, debt) were higher in dollar terms and show a step change in March 2024.
cross_check: IMF AREAER exchange-arrangement classification for the period; no licence-clean parallel-rate series identified.

concept: public debt revisions hidden debt underreporting sovereign debt vintages external domestic
official_series: Public and publicly guaranteed debt stocks, World Bank International Debt Statistics and earlier IMF, UN and League of Nations compilations
what_happened: A paper by Horn, Mihalyi, Nickol and Sosa-Padilla compared 119 editions of League of Nations, UN, IMF and World Bank debt statistics covering up to 187 countries over more than a century.
effect_on_data: They found reported public debt is later revised up by roughly 1% of GDP on average, with revisions often revealed during IMF programmes and defaults, so the latest vintage can still understate debt.
cross_check: Compare successive archived vintages of World Bank International Debt Statistics for the same country and year.
source_name: National Bureau of Economic Research (Working Paper 32947)

concept: household consumption expenditure survey mpce poverty inequality nss withheld data gap
official_series: Household Consumer Expenditure Survey (NSS 75th round), National Statistical Office (MoSPI)
what_happened: On 15 November 2019 MoSPI said it would not release the July 2017-June 2018 consumer expenditure survey, citing divergence from administrative data and doubts about capturing health and education spending.
effect_on_data: There is no official household consumption or poverty benchmark between the 2011-12 survey and the 2022-23 survey released in February 2024; press reports of draft 2017-18 results were never confirmed.
cross_check: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform modelled estimates for India.
source_name: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (via Press Information Bureau)

concept: gdp growth overestimation base year 2011-12 methodology national accounts manufacturing revision
official_series: GDP at constant prices, 2011-12 base series, National Statistics Office (MoSPI)
what_happened: In a June 2019 Harvard CID working paper, former Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian argued that new data sources and methods in the 2011-12 base series overstated growth.
effect_on_data: He estimated average annual growth for 2011-12 to 2016-17 at about 4.5% (95% interval 3.5-5.5%) against an official figure of about 7%, linked in part to how formal manufacturing is measured.
cross_check: Physical activity indicators such as electricity generation (Central Electricity Authority) and RBI bank credit data.
source_name: Center for International Development, Harvard University (Working Paper 354)

concept: special purpose entities spe pass-through fdi balance of payments holding companies
official_series: Balance of payments and international investment position, De Nederlandsche Bank (with Statistics Netherlands)
what_happened: DNB describes SPEs as entities registered in the Netherlands with little or no physical presence, used to hold assets and channel flows within multinational groups, and shows them as a subcategory of sector S.127.
effect_on_data: Totals that include SPEs, notably FDI positions and financial-account flows, are dominated by intra-group pass-through amounts that say little about investment in the Dutch economy.
cross_check: DNB balance-of-payments series with SPEs shown separately, and OECD FDI statistics by ultimate investing country.

concept: cpi inflation rebasing base year food inflation headline consumer prices break
official_series: Consumer Price Index (headline, food and core), National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria
what_happened: NBS rebased the CPI from January 2025, moving the price reference period from 2009 to 2024=100, with 2023 expenditure weights and the COICOP 2018 classification.
effect_on_data: Headline inflation was 24.48% in January 2025 on the new basis against 34.80% for December 2024 on the old one; the drop reflects the change of index, so the two segments are not one series.
cross_check: WFP market food price data for Nigeria on the Humanitarian Data Exchange.

concept: russia statistics suspension methodology changes gdp oil gas output foreign trade
official_series: GDP, industrial production, real incomes and foreign trade, Rosstat and the Bank of Russia
what_happened: Since 2022 Russia has restricted access to statistics, including foreign trade data, and from April 2023 stopped reporting oil and gas output under Federal Law No. 55-FZ of 28 February 2023, which lets the government suspend the release of official statistical indicators.
effect_on_data: Long series are hard to compare because Rosstat changes methods, presentation and frequency, and some revisions altered earlier readings; a 2023 OSW analysis advised treating published figures with great caution.
cross_check: Partner-country mirror trade (UN Comtrade, Eurostat Comext) and electricity data from Ember.

concept: census population undercount post-enumeration survey mid-year estimates denominators per capita
official_series: Census 2022 and Mid-year Population Estimates, Statistics South Africa
what_happened: Statistics South Africa reported a 31% undercount in Census 2022. A June 2024 technical report for the SA Medical Research Council by Moultrie and Dorrington questioned the scale of the adjustment made for it.
effect_on_data: The report suggests the 62.03 million total may be overstated by about one million, with ages 50+ overstated and ages 5-9 understated, and advised against unadjusted mid-year estimates; per-capita ratios inherit this.
cross_check: UN World Population Prospects modelled population estimates.

concept: gdp growth real output national accounts economic activity estimates reliability
official_series: Gross Domestic Product at constant prices, annual growth (National Bureau of Statistics, Tanzania)
what_happened: In December 2017 IMF staff said other indicators pointed to downward pressure on growth and that NBS would revisit its source data. The authorities did not consent to publication of the 2019 Article IV staff report.
effect_on_data: Official real GDP growth of around 7% a year diverged from tax revenue, credit and spending indicators; press reports on the unpublished 2019 IMF draft cited medium-term growth of 4-5%.
cross_check: IMF World Economic Outlook growth estimates for Tanzania, read alongside electricity generation and tax revenue series.

concept: inflation cpi consumer prices item prices basket transparency indexation wages
official_series: Consumer Price Index (2003=100) (Turkish Statistical Institute, TurkStat)
what_happened: TurkStat published average prices of 400-plus individual CPI items from 2003 until its release of 3 May 2022 and stopped from June 2022. On a suit by the DİSK union confederation, the Ankara 6th Administrative Court ordered disclosure on 31 March 2023; the Ankara Regional Administrative Court rejected TurkStat's appeal on 15 September 2023, and the ruling became final in March 2024, per DİSK.
effect_on_data: The item-level prices behind the headline CPI cannot be checked by outside users; the index itself is still published. Wages, pensions and contracts indexed to CPI carry any measurement error in it.
cross_check: Istanbul Chamber of Commerce (ITO) Istanbul retail price index; ENAG estimates exist but their licence terms are unclear.
source_name: DİSK (Confederation of Progressive Trade Unions of Turkey)

concept: labour force survey employment unemployment inactivity response rate sample quality
official_series: Labour Force Survey estimates of employment, unemployment and economic inactivity (Office for National Statistics)
what_happened: ONS temporarily suspended LFS-derived outputs in October 2023 after response fell to 12.7% overall in July-September 2023 (Great Britain). OSR removed their accredited status in November 2023; they returned in February 2024 as official statistics in development.
effect_on_data: Smaller, less representative samples raise sampling error and risk bias in levels and changes. ONS advises three-month estimates read with payroll and claimant data; the Transformed LFS is not expected to replace it before 2027.
cross_check: HMRC PAYE Real Time Information payrolled employees, published by ONS under the Open Government Licence.

concept: inflation cpi consumer prices missing month shutdown imputation rent
official_series: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, CPI-U (Bureau of Labor Statistics)
what_happened: BLS did not collect CPI data from 1 October to 12 November 2025 during the lapse in appropriations and issued no October 2025 CPI release. Only a few indexes built from non-survey data were later published for October.
effect_on_data: Most October 2025 indexes, incl. all items and core, do not exist. October prices were carried forward from September (rents from April 2025), so November one-month changes and rent/OER indexes are affected until April 2026.
cross_check: BEA Personal Consumption Expenditures price index for October and November 2025.

concept: household survey unemployment rate labor force cps missing month shutdown
official_series: Current Population Survey labor force estimates, incl. unemployment rate (Bureau of Labor Statistics)
what_happened: During the lapse in federal appropriations from 1 October to 12 November 2025, BLS suspended all CPS operations. October 2025 data were not collected and were not collected retroactively; no October Employment Situation release was issued.
effect_on_data: There are no October 2025 CPS estimates (shown as a dash in BLS tables); 2025 annual averages and Q4 2025 estimates are affected. Establishment-survey payrolls for October were published with November data.
cross_check: BLS Current Employment Statistics payrolls and state unemployment insurance claims for October 2025.

concept: external debt public debt ppg chinese loans soe arrears debt stock
official_series: Public and publicly guaranteed external debt stocks (World Bank International Debt Statistics; Ministry of Finance, Zambia)
what_happened: A 2021 Johns Hopkins SAIS-CARI briefing paper estimated Zambia's public external debt to Chinese lenders at about US$6.6 billion in August 2021, almost double the highest figure the government had released (US$3.4 billion), and found that SOE external debt had not been reported to the World Bank IDS.
effect_on_data: IDS and Ministry of Finance debt stocks in these vintages appear to omit state-owned enterprise borrowing (e.g. ZESCO) and some Chinese loans, per CARI, understating the stock and misstating its split by creditor.
cross_check: Compare later IDS vintages with earlier ones; the IMF's 2022 ECF request (Country Report 22/292) shows US$5.9 billion of public and publicly guaranteed debt owed to China at end-2021; the Boston University Chinese Loans to Africa database.
source_name: Johns Hopkins SAIS China Africa Research Initiative, Briefing Paper No. 5 (Brautigam and Wang, 2021)

concept: inflation cpi consumer prices annual rate year on year suspension currency
official_series: Consumer Price Index, year-on-year inflation rate (Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency, ZIMSTAT)
what_happened: In the 2019 Mid-Year Budget Review, presented to Parliament on 1 August 2019, the Finance Minister said ZIMSTAT would defer publishing year-on-year inflation for 12 months to February 2020, because the 2019 move from the multicurrency system to the Zimbabwe dollar affected the CPI base; users were to follow month-on-month inflation meanwhile.
effect_on_data: No official annual inflation rate was published for these months. Annual rates must be built by chaining month-on-month prints, and comparisons across the 2019 currency change mix currency regimes.
cross_check: WFP and FEWS NET market food-price monitoring for Zimbabwe.
source_name: Ministry of Finance and Economic Development, Zimbabwe, 2019 Mid-Year Budget Review (paras 54-56; copy hosted by the Commercial Farmers' Union, the Treasury site being unreachable)

concept: gdp growth overestimation national accounts night lights earnings proxy measurement
official_series: Real GDP growth, Ethiopian Statistics Service (formerly Central Statistical Agency)
what_happened: A 2025 report by Ethiopia's Ministry of Finance and the IFS TaxDev centre compared official GDP growth with three alternative indicators of economic activity.
effect_on_data: Reported real GDP grew 60% from 2015/16 to 2022/23 against 28% implied by night lights, and urban earnings were flat; survey consumption matched official growth, so the report did not conclude growth was overstated.
cross_check: VIIRS night-lights from the Earth Observation Group and IMF WEO staff growth estimates.
source_name: Ministry of Finance of Ethiopia and Institute for Fiscal Studies (TaxDev)

concept: fiscal deficit arrears energy sector ipp payables contingent liabilities budget
official_series: Central government fiscal balance and arrears (Ministry of Finance, Ghana)
what_happened: Ghana's Ministry of Finance stated in January 2026 that it paid about US$1.47 billion in 2025 on energy-sector obligations: US$597 million drawn on a World Bank guarantee, about US$480 million in gas invoices, and debts to independent power producers.
effect_on_data: Power-sector payables to gas suppliers and power producers built up outside the central government's own spending lines; deficit figures for the years they accrued do not show them, and their settlement falls in 2025.
cross_check: IMF Extended Credit Facility review reports for Ghana, which tabulate the energy-sector financial shortfall.
source_name: Information Services Department, Government of Ghana

concept: government deficit public debt fiscal statistics edp revision vintage
official_series: Government deficit and debt, Excessive Deficit Procedure notifications (Eurostat; Hellenic Statistical Authority)
what_happened: In October 2009 Greece revised its 2008 government deficit from 5.0% to 7.7% of GDP and its planned 2009 deficit from 3.7% to 12.5%. A European Commission report of January 2010 set out the methodological and institutional problems behind the revisions.
effect_on_data: Greek deficit and debt vintages published before the 2010 revisions understate both; the 2009 deficit was later validated at 15.4% of GDP. Use only the current restated EDP series.
cross_check: Current Eurostat EDP notification tables for Greece (restated series).

concept: crude oil production output opec secondary sources direct communication supply
official_series: Crude oil production, direct communication and secondary sources (OPEC Monthly Oil Market Report)
what_happened: OPEC's Monthly Oil Market Report prints crude production as reported by member countries (direct communication) in a separate table from averaged secondary-source estimates, and some members report no figure. A 2018 KAPSARC paper (Mollet and Al Muhanna) notes that many member governments treat production data as confidential or publish figures analysts consider unreliable.
effect_on_data: Country-reported and secondary-source crude figures can differ materially for the same country and month (March 2025: Iraq 3,637 tb/d reported against 3,981 from secondary sources); neither is a direct audited measurement.
cross_check: US EIA International Energy Statistics crude oil production estimates.
source_name: OPEC, Monthly Oil Market Report, April 2025 (tables 5-7 and 5-8)

concept: crude oil production condensate liquids opec+ quota compliance output
official_series: Oil and gas condensate production (Ministry of Energy of the Republic of Kazakhstan)
what_happened: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy reports output as oil and gas condensate combined, while its OPEC+ target is compared with crude alone. For March 2025 a deputy energy minister told Argus crude was 1.79 mb/d and condensate 0.29 mb/d, against a 1.468 mb/d target; OPEC's secondary sources put March 2025 crude at 1.852 mb/d.
effect_on_data: Combined figures overstate the crude volume relevant to OPEC+ targets by roughly 0.3 mb/d (2025); crude-only figures understate total liquids supply.
cross_check: JODI's oil database, which reports Kazakhstan's crude and NGL (condensate) separately from 2016 (kz_crude_production, kz_ngl_production); US EIA International Energy Statistics, which report crude including lease condensate and other liquids separately.
source_name: Argus Media (the crude and condensate split is not in an official release)

concept: statistics act publication restrictions independent statistics criminal penalties dissemination nbs approval
official_series: All official statistics, National Bureau of Statistics Tanzania (Statistics Act 2015)
what_happened: The Written Laws (Miscellaneous Amendments) (No. 3) Act 2018 barred disseminating statistics 'intended to invalidate, distort or discredit official statistics' or without the approval of the Statistician General, with a fine of at least TZS 10 million, at least three years' imprisonment, or both. The No. 3 Act of 2019, passed on 27 June 2019, repealed these provisions and the penalty and gave any person the right to publish statistics that differ from official figures.
effect_on_data: No direct change to published official series is documented; the effect was on independent statistics that could be used to check official figures during 2018-2019.
cross_check: IMF Article IV staff estimates and World Bank Tanzania Economic Updates.
source_name: Written Laws (Miscellaneous Amendments) (No. 3) Act 2019, published by the National Bureau of Statistics, Tanzania

concept: bls commissioner leadership institutional independence statistical agency governance
official_series: All releases (Bureau of Labor Statistics)
what_happened: BLS lists Commissioner Erika McEntarfer's tenure as January 2024 to August 2025; she was removed from office by the President on 1 August 2025, per press reports. Deputy Commissioner William Wiatrowski was acting Commissioner from August 2025 to August 2026. Brett Matsumoto, confirmed by the Senate on 7 August 2026, became Commissioner on 11 August 2026.
effect_on_data: No series break is attached to this event. Method and collection changes in this period are documented in separate BLS notices (CPI sample reductions, the October 2025 collection gap).
cross_check: Compare release dates against the published BLS release calendar, and payroll trends against the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages.

concept: nonfarm payrolls employment jobs benchmark revision establishment survey ces
official_series: Current Employment Statistics total nonfarm employment (Bureau of Labor Statistics)
what_happened: On 9 September 2025 BLS published a preliminary benchmark estimate lowering March 2025 total nonfarm employment by 911,000 (-0.6%). The final benchmark, released 11 February 2026, lowered it by 898,000 seasonally adjusted (-862,000, -0.5%, unadjusted).
effect_on_data: Vintages published before February 2026 overstate payroll levels and growth for April 2024 to March 2025, by about 0.9 million jobs at March 2025. Use post-benchmark vintages for this period.

official_series: Consumer Price Index, area and item indexes (Bureau of Labor Statistics)
what_happened: BLS suspended CPI price collection entirely in Lincoln NE and Provo UT from April 2025 and Buffalo NY from June 2025, and suspended about 15% of the sample on average in the other 72 areas, stating that resources could no longer support the collection.
effect_on_data: More prices are imputed. BLS states the effect on all-items CPI-U and CPI-W is minimal, but subnational and item-level indexes may be more volatile, and it had not measured that effect.

concept: household survey response rate nonresponse unemployment rate cps sample quality
official_series: Current Population Survey household response rate and labor force estimates (Bureau of Labor Statistics)
what_happened: BLS data show the CPS response rate fell from about 90% in early 2013 to about 82% in early 2020 and 67-70% in 2024-25. It was 64.0% in November 2025 after the shutdown and 65.7% in September 2026.
effect_on_data: Lower response raises sampling error and the risk of nonresponse bias in household-survey estimates such as the unemployment rate; the response rate itself does not measure that bias.
cross_check: BLS Current Employment Statistics payrolls, Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages and state unemployment insurance claims.
